title: Why Do We Sneeze?
hook: Your nose just launched a tiny hurricane…
narration: Your nose just launched a tiny hurricane.
Whoosh! That blast of air is a sneeze.
A sneeze is your body’s fast way to say: something does not belong in here.
Maybe a speck of dust floated in from the air around you.
Dust is dry and tiny, like crumbs riding on the wind.
Or tiny pollen from a flower landed inside your nose.
Pollen is a yellow powder plants use to grow more flowers.
It isn’t trying to be mean. It just tickles.
So your body takes a big breath… then air blasts out to clear the path.
That air can race out faster than a car on a city street.
That’s why a sneeze feels so sudden and so strong.
Then you can breathe easy again. Your nose did its job.
Cover your sneeze with your elbow so the spray stays with you.
And remember: next time you sneeze, that’s your body being a tiny superhero for your lungs.
